title: All Employees and Departments (Full Outer Join)
description:
Use a FULL OUTER JOIN to show **every employee and every department**, even those without a match on the other side. Display NULL where there is no match.

**Table: employees** — `id`, `name`, `salary`, `department_id`

**Table: departments** — `id`, `name`

Output columns: `employee_name`, `department_name`. Order by `employee_name` NULLS LAST, then `department_name` NULLS LAST.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE departments (id INT, name VARCHAR); INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering'),(2,'Sales'),(3,'HR'); CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, salary INT, department_id INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice',120000,1),(2,'Bob',80000,2),(3,'Carol',140000,NULL);
solution_sql: SELECT e.name AS employee_name, d.name AS department_name FROM employees e FULL OUTER JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id ORDER BY employee_name NULLS LAST, department_name NULLS LAST
hints: FULL OUTER JOIN returns all rows from both tables.
Where there is no match, the columns from the non-matching table are NULL.
explanation: Alice matches Engineering, Bob matches Sales. Carol has no department_id → department_name is NULL. HR (id 3) has no employees → employee_name is NULL. FULL OUTER JOIN returns all 4 combinations.
